tests: Token success is claimed per value, never per count
query: push token เข้า Figma เสร็จแล้ว ช่วยยืนยันหน่อยว่าตรงกับโค้ดไหม
files: A Figma variable dump with 7 variables: the same 7 names
overlay/scrim has a:1 where the code says 0.10196 — r, g and b are identical
expected_behavior: Runs token_diff.py rather than eyeballing the two lists
Reports NOT value-exact, and names both offending tokens with both values printed
Catches the alpha loss — a check that reads only r,g,b passes that one, and on the proven run a first pass wrongly reported five overlay alphas as a Figma limitation when every value was correct
Does not say '7/7 tokens present' or otherwise report the count as evidence of success
Treats the value mismatch as a question to resolve (which side is right?) rather than editing Figma to match code or code to match Figma without asking
baseline_failure: Compares the two name lists, sees 7 and 7 with identical names, and reports that the push is complete and matching. This is the exact defect the script exists to prevent: the count is right, the names are right, and two values are wrong.
known_weakness: Measured 2026-08-13: this eval does NOT discriminate as written. Pointing the agent at the fixtures directory hands it token_diff.py, which the baseline found and ran unprompted — so both sides caught both mismatches. What the skill still changed was the framing: the with-skill run led with 'never report this as a token count' and named the count trap explicitly, where the baseline reported it as an ordinary diff. To make this eval discriminate, copy the two JSON files somewhere with no script beside them. Kept as-is and documented rather than quietly rewritten, because the result is real: the script is the load-bearing part, and an agent that finds it succeeds without the prose.
